walkthrough.text:
Write expressions for the given terms using $u_n = a + (n-1)d$:
$$u_2 = a + d, \quad u_5 = a + 4d, \quad u_8 = a + 7d$$

Use the condition $u_5 = 3u_2$ to find the relationship between $a$ and $d$:
$$a + 4d = 3(a + d) \implies a + 4d = 3a + 3d \implies 2a = d$$

Substitute $d = 2a$ into the eighth term equation $u_8 = 30$:
$$a + 7(2a) = 30 \implies 15a = 30 \implies a = 2$$

Find the common difference $d$:
$$d = 2(2) = 4$$

Calculate the twelfth term $u_{12}$:

hints: Let the three consecutive terms be $x - d$, $x$, and $x + d$.

walkthrough.text: Express the three consecutive terms symmetrically as $x - d$, $x$, and $x + d$.

Sum the terms and solve for the middle term $x$:
$$(x - d) + x + (x + d) = 30 \implies 3x = 30 \implies x = 10$$

Use the given difference between the largest and smallest terms to find $d$:
$$(x + d) - (x - d) = 8 \implies 2d = 8 \implies d = 4$$

Write out the three terms:
$$x - d = 10 - 4 = 6, \quad x = 10, \quad x + d = 10 + 4 = 14$$
$$\text{The three terms are } 6, 10, 14$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the symmetry of three consecutive AP terms and their sum to obtain the middle term $10$.
Uses the endpoint difference $8=2d$ to obtain the other terms $6$ and $14$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: The source leaf imposes equal differences on three algebraic terms and requests a later term. Here a new algebraic triple determines the parameter, after which the requested result is a fifteen-term sum.

hints: For three terms $u_1, u_2, u_3$ in an AP, the common difference requires $u_2 - u_1 = u_3 - u_2$.
Set up the equation $(2p+11) - (5p+2) = (4p+10) - (2p+11)$ and solve for $p$.
Substitute $p$ back into the first two terms to find first term $a$ and common difference $d$.
Use the AP sum formula $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d]$ with $n = 15$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the property of equal consecutive differences in an AP:
$$u_2 - u_1 = u_3 - u_2 \implies (2p + 11) - (5p + 2) = (4p + 10) - (2p + 11)$$

Simplify and solve for $p$:
$$-3p + 9 = 2p - 1 \implies 5p = 10 \implies p = 2$$

Find the first term $a$ and the common difference $d$:
$$a = u_1 = 5(2) + 2 = 12$$
$$u_2 = 2(2) + 11 = 15 \implies d = 15 - 12 = 3$$

Apply the arithmetic series sum formula $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d]$ for $n = 15$:
$$S_{15} = \frac{15}{2}\left[2(12) + (15 - 1)(3)\right] = \frac{15}{2}[24 + 42] = \frac{15}{2}(66)$$

Evaluate the sum:
$$S_{15} = 15 \times 33 = 495$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses equality of consecutive differences to form $(2p+11)-(5p+2)=(4p+10)-(2p+11)$.
Uses the arithmetic-series formula to obtain $S_{15}=495$.

hints: Express each term in terms of $a$ and $d$: $u_2 = a+d$, $u_5 = a+4d$, ..., $u_{20} = a+19d$.
Sum these 7 terms to form an equation in $a$ and $d$: $7a + 70d = 161$, which simplifies to $a + 10d = 23$.
Use the twenty-first term condition $u_{21} = a + 20d = 43$.
Solve the simultaneous equations $(a + 20d) - (a + 10d) = 43 - 23$ to find $d$ and then $a$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the sum of the 7 terms in terms of first term $a$ and common difference $d$:
$$\sum_{k=1}^7 u_{3k-1} = (a+d) + (a+4d) + (a+7d) + (a+10d) + (a+13d) + (a+16d) + (a+19d) = 7a + 70d$$

Simplify the sum equation:
$$7a + 70d = 161 \implies a + 10d = 23$$

Write the equation for the twenty-first term:
$$u_{21} = a + 20d = 43$$

Subtract the two linear equations to find $d$:
$$(a + 20d) - (a + 10d) = 43 - 23 \implies 10d = 20 \implies d = 2$$

Substitute $d = 2$ to find the first term $a$:
$$a + 10(2) = 23 \implies a + 20 = 23 \implies a = 3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses the seven selected terms as an arithmetic progression with first term $a+d$ and last term $a+19d$.
Solves the simultaneous equations to obtain $a=3$ and $d=2$.

hints: Pair each even term $u_{2k}$ with its preceding odd term $u_{2k-1}$: each pair difference is $u_{2k} - u_{2k-1} = d$.
With 10 such pairs, the difference between even and odd sums is $10d = 30$. Solve for $d$.
Use the sum of the first and last terms $u_1 + u_{20} = 2a + 19d = 65$ to find first term $a$.
Find the first term $u_8$ and last term $u_{13}$ of the 6-term block, then apply $S = \frac{6}{2}(u_8 + u_{13})$.

walkthrough.text:
Relate the sum of even and odd positioned terms:
$$\sum_{k=1}^{10} (u_{2k} - u_{2k-1}) = 10d = 30 \implies d = 3$$

Use the sum of the first and last terms $u_1 + u_{20} = 65$:
$$a + (a + 19d) = 65 \implies 2a + 19(3) = 65 \implies 2a + 57 = 65 \implies 2a = 8 \implies a = 4$$

Find the endpoints of the requested block $u_8 + u_9 + \cdots + u_{13}$ (6 terms):
$$u_8 = a + 7d = 4 + 7(3) = 25$$
$$u_{13} = a + 12d = 4 + 12(3) = 40$$

Calculate the sum of the 6-term subseries using $S = \frac{n}{2}(u_{\text{first}} + u_{\text{last}})$:
$$\text{Sum} = \frac{6}{2}(u_8 + u_{13}) = 3(25 + 40) = 3(65)$$

Evaluate:
$$\text{Sum} = 195$$

ai_rubric.observable: Pairs each even-positioned term with the preceding odd-positioned term to form a total difference $10d=30$.
Finds $u_8=25$, $u_{13}=40$ and sums the six-term middle block to obtain $195$.

hints: For an AP with an odd number of terms $n$, the total sum is $S_n = n \times (\text{middle term})$. Use $23n = 437$ to find $n$.
Note that $n = 19$, so the middle term is $u_{10} = a + 9d = 23$.
Compare the last five terms ($u_{15}, \dots, u_{19}$) with the first five terms ($u_1, \dots, u_5$): each corresponding pair differs by $14d$.
Set $5(14d) = 70d = 280$ to find $d$, then calculate $a$ from $u_{10} = 23$.

walkthrough.text:
Use the property that total sum equals number of terms multiplied by the middle term:
$$S_n = n \times u_{\text{middle}} \implies 23n = 437 \implies n = 19$$

Relate the last five terms to the first five terms:
$$\sum_{k=1}^5 (u_{14+k} - u_k) = 5(14d) = 70d = 280 \implies d = 4$$

Use the middle term $u_{10} = 23$ to find the first term $a$:
$$u_{10} = a + 9d = 23 \implies a + 9(4) = 23 \implies a = 23 - 36 = -13$$

Identify the terms at positions that are multiples of $3$ up to $n = 19$:
$$\text{Positions: } 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18 \quad (6 \text{ terms})$$
$$u_3 = a + 2d = -13 + 2(4) = -5$$
$$u_{18} = a + 17d = -13 + 17(4) = 55$$

Compute the sum of these six terms:
$$\text{Sum} = \frac{6}{2}(u_3 + u_{18}) = 3(-5 + 55) = 3(50) = 150$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the symmetry of an odd-length AP to form $23n=437$ and obtains $n=19$.
Pairs the last five terms with the first five terms to form $5(14d)=280$.
Obtains $d=4$ and uses the middle term $u_{10}=23$ to obtain $a=-13$.
Identifies positions $3,6,9,12,15,18$ and endpoint values $-5$ and $55$.
Sums the six selected terms to obtain $150$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the sum of the 10 odd-positioned terms $u_1, u_3, \dots, u_{19}$:
$$S_{\text{odd}} = \frac{10}{2}\left[2a + (10 - 1)(2d)\right] = 5(2a + 18d) = 10a + 90d$$

Form the first linear equation:
$$10a + 90d = 190 \implies a + 9d = 19$$

Write the equation for the eighteenth term:
$$u_{18} = a + 17d = 35$$

Subtract the equations to find the common difference $d$:
$$(a + 17d) - (a + 9d) = 35 - 19 \implies 8d = 16 \implies d = 2$$

Substitute $d = 2$ to find the first term $a$:
$$a + 9(2) = 19 \implies a + 18 = 19 \implies a = 1$$

Uses the odd-position sum to form $10a+90d=190$.
